newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals ease on dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Regionals ease on dollar strength.

text.p: * Regional currencies under pressure from dollar rise versus majors after news of Italy's re-entry into Exchange Rate Mechanism.
* Indonesian rupiah eases on ample liquidity, with upward pressure seen. Support pegged at 2,344/45 and resistance at 2,347/48.
* Baht hit by firmer dollar/majors. Support seen at 23.443/44.
* Malaysian ringgit eases on heavy dollar/mark buying by U.S. funds.
Regional currencies were hit by the dollar's gains against the majors on Monday after news of Italy's re-entry into the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
In Indonesia, dealers said ample liquidity also weighed on the rupiah, causing players to buy the dollar and sell forward swaps down.
Spot rupiah fell to 2,346.00/47.00 at 0450 GMT from the open of 2,343.50/44.50 on sustained bullish dollar sentiment.
Overnight swap declined to 0.22/0.26 from 0.25/0.35 points on flush money market liquidity, dealers said.
One local bank dealer in Jakarta said cheap local funds continued to sustain further buying interest in the dollar.
"The buying is seen driven mainly by local operators, which forces offshore operators to reduce short dollar positions," he said, adding that the momentum was still prevalent.
"We are now some points above the central bank band. There is more room to trade now. We believe the central bank would not widen the band in the medium-term," the dealer said.
One economist said earlier the present central bank depreciation policy suggested that it did not plan to widen its band in the medium-term.
Offshore operators had been putting pressure by going short on the dollar, triggering speculation of another band widening by the central bank on the back of heavy capital inflows.
But the central bank has been resisting the pressure and had even challenged the market.
The local bank dealer said he would maintain a long dollar position as long as the central bank maintained its three- to four point rupiah depreciation each week.

Another dealer said operators were also seen buying dollars in anticipation of narrowing interest rate differentials between the dollar and the rupiah after the central bank seemed to loosen its monetary policy recently.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,340/2,532 and the conversion rate to 2,340/2,388 on Friday.
In Thailand, concern over the new finance ministry post weighed on the baht. It was quoted at 25.443-25.447 to the dollar at 0450 GMT.
Dealers said dollar/baht was likely to be dictated by the dollar/majors, mainly the dollar/mark after mark/lira weakened on Italy's re-entry into the ERM.

They said the market ignored the Thai central bank governor's call on banks to cut their minimum loan rates to boost the economy, but instead focused on the new cabinet lineup. Activity was also driven by this month's reserve requirement.
"Banks began to keep funds for the next reserve requirement. The interbank rate is likely to stand above 10 percent this week," said one dealer at a foreign bank in Bangkok.
"I think the market is expecting liquidity to tighten due to the maintenance period and this is supporting the six month-forward rate at the 44/45 level," a Singapore dealer said.
In Malaysia, the ringgit broke out of its recent range to head south on heavy dollar/mark buying in early Tokyo, dealers said.
They said the ringgit was just tracking the trend in major currencies and was likely to ease further.
"There is too much pressure. It is hard to be short dollar this morning," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in Singapore.
Dealers said the dollar faced resistance at the 2.5220 level, which if broken, could see the ringgit falling to 2.5280.
"Ringgit is expected to retreat for a while, if not today, in the next few days. So it is a good opportunity to buy dollars at any dip," a dealer with a Kuala Lumpur bank said.
At 0450 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5235/45 to the dollar against 2.5194/04 late on Friday.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Angela Tan in Singapore (65-8703080)
